findings.description: The partial-review branch returns `pr/ci-pending` before the `pr/ci-failing` check runs. A quick or area-restricted `@claude review` that finds no importants therefore labels a PR with failing checks as pending, which breaks the documented `pr/ci-failing > pr/ci-pending` order.

The `hasOpenBotThread` comment says it finds "the newest bot-opened, unresolved review thread, as `ci-wait.service.ts` reads them". The function returns true for any unresolved `github-actions` thread from any run. `ci-wait.service.ts` reads no threads. The reader that does, `github.client.ts` (~387-394), keeps only the newest run's threads. Reword it to "any run's unresolved bot thread counts", or delete it.

The PR body says "A crashed review is `failure` and stays `pr/ci-failing`". That holds only when no earlier round left an unresolved bot thread. Otherwise `hasOpenBotThread` returns `pr/review-open` even when the review status is `failure`. The behavior follows from the new ranking, but the body should say so.

The last sentence of the review-open comment, "The description covers the round just posted.", only restates the left half of the `||`. Per AGENTS.md §Comments it can go. The rest of the comment is a real WHY.
The `pr/ci-pending` label description, "Checks are still running", now also covers a partial review where nothing is running. Consider "Checks are still running or the review was only partial".
